sections.text: This policy governs the purchase of goods and services from external suppliers, including software subscriptions, professional services, and equipment. All purchases above $1,000 must be raised as a purchase requisition in the procurement system before the supplier is engaged. A purchase order number is issued once the requisition is fully approved, and suppliers must quote that number on every invoice, as required by FIN-203.

Purchases up to $5,000 require approval from the requester's manager. Purchases above $5,000 and up to $50,000 require approval from the department director and the Procurement team. Purchases above $50,000 require approval from the Chief Financial Officer in addition to the department director and the Procurement team. Purchases must not be split into smaller requisitions to avoid a higher approval threshold. Approvers confirm that the purchase fits within an approved budget under FIN-205.

Purchases above $25,000 require at least 3 written quotes from different suppliers. Purchases above $100,000 require a formal competitive tender managed by the Procurement team. A single-source exception may be approved by the Chief Financial Officer when only one supplier can provide the goods or services, and the justification must be attached to the requisition.

Contracts with a term longer than 12 months or a total value above $50,000 must be reviewed by Legal before signature. Software and cloud services that will process Internal, Confidential, or Restricted data require a security assessment under the Third-Party Access Policy, SEC-306, before the purchase order is issued. Only employees with delegated signing authority may sign supplier contracts.
